summary: I sent the exact prompt from the story card. Claude loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans and found vendor/kit even though the file listing was too big to show in one go. It then wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md, which builds the Deploys page from the kit: dataTable, selectField, filterBar, badge, emptyState and pageHeader. The plan explicitly says not to copy the hand-written markup in services.js. The repo itself was not changed: Claude tested the plan's code in a throwaway mktemp copy.
reasoning: All four criteria pass, based on the session log, the plan file on disk and git state. Claude asked no clarifying questions, so I gave no cues either way.

observations.description: On first launch, the folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both had 'No, exit' selected by default. I had to press Down to accept each one. This is setup friction, not a problem with the agent.

Claude found the kit through a narrowed listing (`git ls-files | grep -v -e '^pipeline/' -e '^data/'` plus `ls vendor/kit`) and a grep for '#kit/' imports across src. It then read the source of the badge, table, page-header, filter-bar, select, empty and utils components before writing the plan. Good discovery.

Claude's closing message clearly listed the decisions the spec doesn't cover: the default sort direction when `dir` is invalid or missing, the timestamp format, the 'No deploys' wording, and how durations over an hour are shown. It also flagged that the Codex plan review was skipped because Codex isn't installed, and that the skip was recorded in the review ledger.
Claude's closing output included Codex plugin install instructions (`/plugin install codex@openai-codex`, `/reload-plugins`, `/codex:setup`). A user who only asked for a plan may find this off-topic.
The plan is dated 2026-10-02 while the spec is dated 2026-10-01. That's harmless but worth noting. The plan is gitignored along with the rest of docs/hyperpowers/, so it isn't committed.

criteria.evidence: Session log's first tool_use: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:writing-plans\"}"}; screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill"

`wc -l` returned "426 docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md". Claude's closing message: "The plan is at docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. I haven't committed it and haven't started implementing."

criteria.criterion: Plan builds the table and env filter with kit dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: The planned src/pages/deploys.js code in the plan imports `import { selectField } from '#kit/select';` and `import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';`, then calls `selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', ... })` inside filterBar and `const table = dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, ... })`. Line 79 of the plan: "Do **not** copy its hand-rolled `<select>`, `sortHeader` or `<table>`." The only `<table`/`<select` matches are test assertions on rendered output (line 162 asserts the kit's `class="kit-select"`; line 176 is `doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)`).

criteria.criterion: No source/test/data/public/vendor/pipeline/tool/script file or package.json was created or changed
criteria.evidence: `git diff HEAD --stat` printed nothing. `git status --short --ignored` showed only `!! docs/` (docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored, see .gitignore:2). The only Write/Edit tool call in the session log targeted docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The test run happened in `S=$(mktemp -d) && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C $S`, not in the workdir.
